actions.body: Maintaining continuity across multiple turns of execution is one of the central challenges in autonomous agent design. Without persistent state tracking and structured verification gates, agents operating across organizational boundaries encounter severe accountability gaps. Recent architectural developments introduce Verification State Architectures (VSAs) that track hypotheses, gates, and evidence pointers, ensuring that execution traces remain verifiable and bound to durable state rather than ephemeral transcripts. By combining these structural safeguards with rigorous causal-mechanistic testing, intelligent systems can bridge the gap between declared intent and observed behavior. Summary: This research explores how structured state architectures help AI agents maintain accountability and consistency across multiple execution turns.
